exam: How does uterine atony differ from retained placental tissue on examination? — Atony: boggy, enlarged uterus; retained tissue: firm uterus with palpable tissue.
Why is ergometrine contraindicated in a patient with pre‑eclampsia? — It causes severe hypertension and vasoconstriction, worsening maternal risk.
What alternative uterotonic can be used if oxytocin is unavailable and the patient is HIV‑positive? — Misoprostol rectally; safe in HIV and does not require refrigeration.
A patient on magnesium sulfate for eclampsia develops PPH. Which uterotonic choice is safest? — Oxytocin; magnesium potentiates the effect of other uterotonics and may cause hypotension.
Explain the rationale for giving tranexamic acid in postpartum hemorrhage. — It blocks plasminogen activation, stabilizing clots and reducing ongoing bleeding.
When should you consider surgical intervention for uterine atony? — If bleeding persists after uterotonics, massage, and balloon tamponade, proceed to uterine artery ligation or hysterectomy.
ai.title: Uterine Atony
ai.subject: Obstetrics & gynaecology
ai.summary: Uterine atony is the failure of the uterus to contract after delivery, leading to postpartum hemorrhage. Prompt recognition, assessment of severity, and targeted management are essential, especially in low‑resource settings.

b: Most common cause of primary postpartum hemorrhage (PPH)
sections.p: After placental delivery the myometrium should contract to compress uterine vessels. When this contractile response is insufficient, bleeding persists, defining uterine atony.

t.b: Determines if uterus is boggy (atrophic) versus firm (normal); guides immediate uterotonic therapy

b: Risk factors: prolonged labor, multiple gestation, macrosomia, uterine over‑distension, chorioamnionitis, anemia, use of magnesium sulfate, herbal uterine relaxants
sections.p: Uterine atony results from impaired myometrial contractility, often due to over‑distension, infection, or pharmacologic factors.

t.b: Detects acute anemia; falling values indicate ongoing blood loss
Confirms retained placental tissue or uterine inversion as alternative causes of bleeding

b: First‑line uterotonics: oxytocin, misoprostol (if oxytocin unavailable)
Second‑line: ergometrine (avoid in hypertension), carboprost (avoid in asthma), tranexamic acid
sections.p: In low‑resource East African hospitals, delayed recognition of atony contributes to maternal mortality. Early uterotonic use and simple mechanical measures can be lifesaving.
